A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ET-SEED and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. All 20 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2 support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices E and H–J report original simulation, real-robot, ablation and network-training results.

after.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 retain original simulation, real-robot and ablation results. Appendix D includes both the retained single-step experiment and a new multi-step convergence experiment.

M1.justification: The specified denoiser changes from predicting individual actions using (O, H_i; k, i) to predicting an entire sequence using (O, A; k). Algorithms 1–2 change accordingly, and v2 Appendix E expands backbone output dimensions by the trajectory horizon relative to v1 Appendix F. This substantially revises the reported prediction procedure while retaining the invariant-then-equivariant schedule.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same six simulated and four real-robot manipulation tasks, including training and new-pose settings. The added multi-step diagnostic retains the randomly rotated point-cloud domain and changes the diffusion procedure rather than introducing new data or manipulation-task coverage.

E2.justification: DP3, DP3+Aug, EquiBot and the original component ablations remain. Appendix D.2 adds an evaluated all-P3Net diffusion chain, labeled Pure Eqv, as a comparator to the mixed P1Net/P2Net chain; this process-level comparison is absent from v1.

E3.justification: The new multi-step experiment uses equal numbers of training sequences, supervision at every transition and final-output loss plotted against training epochs. Existing robot evaluation settings, including demonstration counts, T/NP testing, augmentation, metrics and real-robot trial counts, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix D.2 tests whether the learning advantage persists across a complete diffusion chain, extending v1's single-step network comparison. The Open Door component ablations are unchanged and merely move from v1 Appendix J to v2 Section 5.1.

E5.justification: Both report simulation averages over five random seeds and success-rate standard deviations. V2 introduces no additional stated run counts, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures; shaded learning curves were already present in v1.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 6 adds convergence curves showing faster learning for Inv+Eqv than Pure Eqv in the new multi-step experiment. Simulation scores, real-robot scores, component-ablation values and single-step losses match across versions after relocation and renumbering.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the invariant-backbone identity in v1 Equation 3 and the transformed-trajectory expression in Definition 3. It also removes v1 Appendix B.2's adjoint definition and associated identities. The central propositions and Markov-kernel argument remain, with the equivariance proof expressed using sequence notation.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central contributions: a trajectory-level SE(3) diffusion policy, a weaker condition for equivariant diffusion, and improved data efficiency and spatial generalization, including real-robot learning from 20 demonstrations. The additional convergence evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2's conclusion explicitly identifies dependence on segmented object point clouds, assumed end-effector reachability through inverse kinematics and controllers, and the inability of its 6D action representation to handle higher-dimensional dexterous manipulation. These applicability limitations were not explicitly discussed together in v1.

D1.justification: V2 documents trajectory-sized backbone outputs and the feature types, timestep conditioning and supervision used in the new multi-step diagnostic. Its abstract also explicitly states code availability at the existing project website, whereas v1 provides a generic website link.

R1.justification: V2 adds Eade's Lie-group background reference and AdaManip, while removing UniGarmentManip and GarmentLab references from the garment-task discussion. The substantive positioning against existing equivariant manipulation and diffusion methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: preliminary background moves into the main text, ablations join the experimental section, the separate equivariance subsection is integrated into the method, and duplicated appendix result discussions are removed. Method explanations are rewritten, and template acknowledgments and author/header information are revised.

P2.justification: Simulation, real-robot and ablation tables move from appendices into the main paper. The aircraft illustration is redesigned as a Markov-chain diagram, Figure 6 adds a convergence plot, and overview graphics and captions are revised. Conference formatting, figure placement and wrapped-table layouts also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new multi-step diagnostic provides more direct support for the efficiency rationale, and the explicit limitations make applicability clearer. Reorganizing background and experimental displays improves accessibility. These are bounded gains: benchmark results remain unchanged and do not establish a performance benefit from the revised sequence-level denoiser.
